transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I guess… I’m here because I don’t feel like work is safe anymore. And I keep thinking there’s something wrong with me now, like I’m not the same person who was doing well there before. It’s hard to explain.
Can you tell me more about why you feel work isn’t safe anymore, and what makes you feel like you’re not the same person?

It’s just… when I’m at work now, I don’t feel like I can trust that things are okay. It feels unsafe, even if I can’t always explain why.

And I keep thinking maybe something in me is… damaged. Like the person who was competent, who got promoted and could handle things, isn’t really there anymore. I don’t like saying that, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you find that this feeling of unease or worry follows you even when you're not at work, like at home or during other parts of your day?

Yeah… it does. Not all the time, but enough.

Like on the train, or even in meetings, I notice I’m checking where the exits are. At lunch with my team I’ll be watching who’s standing too close, or listening for noises in the hallway instead of really following the conversation. It’s… hard to turn off.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, not just work, like things might go wrong or that you won’t be able to handle them?
I don’t know… not really in that general way. It’s more tied to certain situations. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about everything in my life.
Have you ever had sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?
I’m not sure. I mean… I get really tense sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it a sudden episode like that. I haven’t really noticed the sweating or not being able to breathe kind of thing.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most of the time in certain situations, like work or being on the train, even when nothing specific is happening?

Yeah… in those situations, I guess. Like the train, meetings, even lunch sometimes.

I’ll catch myself looking for exits, noticing who’s close to me, listening for stuff in the hallway instead of paying attention. Nothing has to be happening. It’s just… I’m already on edge.
Do you ever feel anxious about being in situations where it might be hard to escape or get help if something happened, like being on the train or in a meeting?

Yeah… I guess that’s part of it. On the train or in meetings, even just lunch with my team, I’m sort of automatically checking where the exits are, who’s too close, things like that.

I keep listening for noises outside the room too, instead of really being there. I don’t know if it’s about escape exactly, but… yeah, it feels hard to relax.
Do you ever avoid going to certain places or situations, like the train or meetings, because of how you feel or the anxiety you’ve described?

Yeah… I do avoid it sometimes. I’ve been trading shifts when I can, or pushing back release windows so I don’t have to be there late.

And if I do go in, I’ll take the side entrance. Or I just work from home if I can. Walking through the lobby after dark is… hard. It feels like I’m going to fall apart.

Can you tell me if you feel that your anxiety in these situations, like on the train or in meetings, is specifically about feeling like you can't escape or might not be able to get help if something happened?

I don’t know if I’d put it that clearly. It’s more like… I’m always checking.

On the train, in meetings, even at lunch, I’m noticing exits, who’s standing too close, listening to the hallway instead of really being there. So… maybe, but I don’t think of it as “can’t escape” in the moment. It’s just what I do.
When you're in those situations, like on the train or in meetings, do you worry that you might have a panic attack or feel extremely anxious and not be able to leave or get help if you needed to?

I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as a panic attack, or like… needing help exactly.

It’s more just that I get tense and want to have a way out. But I don’t know if that’s the same thing.
When you're in those situations, like on the train or in meetings, are you worried that you might start feeling extremely anxious or panicky and not be able to leave or get out?

I’m not really sure. I don’t usually think it through like that.

I just… want to know I can leave if I need to. I don’t know if it’s about getting panicky, exactly.
Have you ever avoided certain places or situations because you were afraid you might feel extremely anxious or panicky and not be able to get out or reach help if you needed to?

I don’t know. I mean… I avoid some things sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s because I think I won’t be able to get help.

It’s more just… if a place feels too closed in or I don’t know how I’d leave, I’d rather not deal with it. I don’t really think past that.
When you avoid places or situations, like the train or meetings, is it because you're afraid you might start feeling extremely anxious or panicky and not be able to leave or get out?
I don’t know if I’d call it that. I’m not really thinking, like, “I’m going to panic.” It’s more just… if I can’t see an easy way to leave, I get uncomfortable and I’d rather avoid it.
When you avoid places or situations like the train or meetings, is it because you're afraid that you might start feeling extremely anxious or panicky and not be able to leave or get out?
I’m not sure. I guess it’s more that I don’t like feeling stuck. I don’t really think it through as “I’m going to panic” or anything… I just want to know I can get out.
When you feel uncomfortable in places like the train or meetings, is it because you're worried you might have a panic attack and not be able to get out or calm down?
I don’t really know. I don’t think of it as a panic attack. It’s just… I don’t like being somewhere I can’t leave easily. That’s about as much as I can say.
When you think ahead of time about being on the train or in a meeting, do you feel anxious beforehand just thinking about being in those situations?
I don’t really know. I mean… sometimes I think about it and don’t feel great, but I’m not sure I’d call it anxiety beforehand. I just kind of avoid thinking about it if I can.
When you know you're going to be on the train or in a meeting ahead of time, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worked up just thinking about it, or dreading it before you even get there?
I guess… maybe a little sometimes, but I don’t really sit there dreading it in a clear way. I mostly try not to think about it until I have to.
When you know you’ll have to be on the train or in a meeting later, do you find yourself feeling anxious or tense just thinking about it before you even get there?
I’m not really sure. I don’t notice it as some clear anxious feeling beforehand. I mostly just… try not to think about it until I’m actually there.
When you know you'll have to be somewhere like the train or a meeting later in the day, do you ever start feeling anxious or tense just thinking about it, even before you get there?
I don’t think so… not in a way I really notice. I might get kind of quiet or put it out of my mind, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there anxious about it beforehand.
When you feel anxious or tense in places like the train or meetings, is it mainly because you feel like it would be hard to get out or reach a safe place if you needed to?

Not exactly that I can’t get out… it’s more like I’m checking everything. On the train or in meetings I notice where the exits are, who’s standing too close, sounds in the hallway. It’s hard to just focus.
